svg.title: AI Factory onion architecture
svg.desc: A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes Azure. Illustrative animation; times are measured where marked, otherwise estimated.

g.text: A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
A lifecycle request travels from the outside in. Each layer calls only the layer inside it, and only the core, Azure Resource Manager,
changes Azure. The outer layers are thin and quick to change; the inner layers do the slow work.
Outer layers are fast to change. Inner layers are slow to run.
Private Function on Flex Consumption that offers the 6 scenarios as
reviewed REST operations and follows the GitHub runs.

management.azure.com: deployments, resource groups, resources, role
The only layer that changes Azure. Most wall-clock time is spent here:
networks, VPN gateway, private endpoints and DNS zones.
e.g. group and subscription deployments · resource-group deletes · provider
Lifecycle path: Consumer > L1 > L2 > L3 pipeline > L4 Bicep > L5 (COMMON, PROJECT, scale sets, deletes)
Bootstrap path: L2 > L3 API-called helpers > L5, skipping L4 (repository-initialization … publication)
A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
An Azure Function enters through the SDK.
The lifecycle Function offers the six scenarios as reviewed REST operations. It never calls the Factory API over the network: it
dispatches aif-ops.yml to a management runner, which calls AzureFactoryClient next to the API.

A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
CLI, SDK and wizards are thin clients.
The azurefactory CLI and Python SDK (purple), the Tkinter wizard (pink) and the MAUI ESAIF.ConfigWizard send the same review,
confirm and status calls. They hold no deployment logic, so they spend seconds, not minutes.
Clients review, confirm and poll. Deciding happens in layer 2.

A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
The FastAPI routes and the service layer behind them build the catalog, reviews, whole-workflow consent, frozen deployment plans,
cost previews and recoveries. State is DPAPI-sealed SQLite on the admin VM, where the identity, VPN and runner are.
A runtime review took 13 min and its confirmation 18 min (measured).

A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
The API starts scripts and pipelines.
The API runs purple Bash and PowerShell such as GHA-update-aifactory-and-run-project.sh, create-new-aifactory-scaleset.sh and
runner-registration.ps1, and dispatches factory-lifecycle.yml or the ADO pipeline on the factory's self-hosted runner.
A COMMON run reached the worker after 3-4 min (measured, aif-125).

1 · L3 Pipelines + API-called scripts > L4 Bicep + pipeline-called scripts: worker bootstrap/lib/factory_lifecycle.py
A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
The worker compiles and deploys purple Bicep: 11-rgCommon, 12-networkCommon and 13-rgLevel for COMMON, 31-network to
11-integration for a project. The pipelines also run scripts such as preflight.sh, subnetCalc_v2.ps1 and delete-services-if-disabled.sh.
Build, preflight and what-if take minutes, not hours (estimated).

A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
ARM creates, updates and deletes resource groups and resources. Networking dominates: a VPN gateway alone takes tens of
minutes, and private endpoints and private DNS zones add more.
Most wall-clock time is spent in the core.

Scenario 1's bootstrap stages, repository-initialization to publication, run on the API host: pink plus vendored purple helpers call az, gh
and git straight to ARM. Only COMMON, PROJECT and later operations go through the pipelines and Bicep.
Bootstrap took 103-131 min on two factories (measured, aif-124 and aif-125).

1 · L2 Factory REST API > L3 Pipelines + API-called scripts: bootstrap stage helpers
2 · L3 Pipelines + API-called scripts > L5 Azure Resource Manager: az, gh, git with the VM's identity
A lifecycle request travels from the outside in, and each layer calls only the layer inside it. Only the core, Azure Resource Manager, changes
Estimated wall-clock time: Init AI Factory 3.3-3.8 h, Add scale set 1.7-2.5 h, Add or update project 0.8-1.6 h, Delete project 20-54 min,
Delete scale set 0.7-1.6 h, Delete AI Factory 0.9-2.3 h. Deletes ran simulated only.
Inner layers cost the most time to change: prevent their bugs instead of looping faster.

Where the time goes: minutes per scenario, by layer
Upper value of each layer's range, stacked; the range total is on the right. Scenarios 4-6 ran simulated only.
Lifecycle path: Consumer > L1 > L2 > L3 pipeline > L4 Bicep > L5 (COMMON, PROJECT, scale sets, deletes)
Bootstrap path: L2 > L3 API-called helpers > L5, skipping L4 (repository-initialization … publication)
2 · L1 Clients > L2 Factory REST API: review + confirm
3 · L2 Factory REST API > L3 Pipelines + API-called scripts: dispatch
4 · L3 Pipelines + API-called scripts > L4 Bicep + pipeline-called scripts: worker
5 · L4 Bicep + pipeline-called scripts > L5 Azure Resource Manager: deploy
